briefdescription.para: Default construction; the interface itself carries no state.

detaileddescription.para: Base is the shared blueprint (an "abstract base class") for every entity in the server. It declares the five SQL statement builders that each concrete entity must supply: create, read, update, delete and search. It also provides a small helper called Binder that safely turns values into numbered placeholders, so data is never pasted into SQL text. The class stores no data of its own; it only fixes the shape that all derived entity classes follow.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: This is the bottom contract of the whole entity layer. Controllers call the five getSql* functions through a Base reference without caring which concrete table is involved, and every concrete entity (Entity, Client, Service, Appointment, Case and friends) inherits from Base. Without it there would be no single way to ask "give me the SQL for this operation", and the safe binding pattern would have to be copied into every table class by hand.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
std::optional: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/optional
Abstract base class / pure virtual function: a function ending in "= 0" forces every child class to implement it, so callers can use one common interface for all of them.
SQL parameter binding: put $1, $2, ... markers in the SQL and pass the real values separately, so user data can never change the meaning of the query; see https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp or the libpqxx documentation.
